analysis: This PR changes only developer documentation (docs/developer/test.md), and the changed ranges fall in the "Add-On Hold" section (base lines 770-784, head 770-788). No runtime code, auth, crypto or deployment settings change. Per the patch excerpt, the section now says the load-fence and managed Super cases load synthetic tiny weights through MLX and need the staged test metallib. The swift test --filter list gains AddonHoldLoadFence, anAddonHoldRetiresTheSuperSlotButKeepsItsPreloadPlan and aFIFOInPlaceOfARequestIsIgnoredWithoutBlocking. The patch excerpt is truncated; the full head text of the changed table rows was not supplied, and I reviewed the base text of all of the file. Security-relevant observations: (1) The documented FIFO-record-refused-without-blocking test relates to T-059 / TB-012 (local DoS via the add-on hold socket/record): a same-UID process planting a FIFO at the hold record path must not block the provider. The doc records test coverage for this, which is a positive signal, not a regression. (2) The doc keeps explicit statements that the peer check is only negatively tested, that physical add-on interoperation is a separate check, and that tests must use isolated state and never touch production. (3) The docs make no new qualification or deployment claims. The remaining question for integration is whether the actual tests and source (the AddonHoldStore FIFO handling and the hold-loop unload/preload-plan behavior) exist as described. That is outside the supplied evidence, and it is a documentation-accuracy question rather than a security regression. No finding is raised.
